messages:
maya: quick sync — onboarding Lumen-13B to catalog. I uploaded weights to s3://redwood-models/lumen-13b/v1/weights.pt and tokenizer to s3://redwood-models/lumen-13b/v1/tokenizer.json + merges. Before I open the model PR can someone sanity-check serving config + known tokenizer oddities? saw OOMs when bs>8 on a 48GB A100.

samir: thanks — noted. are you doing fp16 baseline or starting with q4_0? also can you paste the model.yaml snippet (especially max_batch_tokens / micro_batch_size / kv_cache config)? :eyes:

maya: fp16 baseline first. snippet below (short):
```yaml
model: lumen-13b
weights: s3://redwood-models/lumen-13b/v1/weights.pt
tokenizer: s3://redwood-models/lumen-13b/v1/tokenizer.json
device: cuda:0
max_seq_len: 2048
# current defaults we used in smoke
max_batch_tokens: 8192
micro_batch_size: 8
kv_cache: true
```
Note: tokenizer seems to include a non-ascii pad token '<▁pad>' and lower_case=false. Also small repro: tokenizing "Hello\nWorld" produces a trailing empty token sometimes.

li: short checklist: 1) confirm tokenizers.fast flag — our fast tokenizer sometimes collapses weird special tokens. try setting tokenizers.fast=false in model yaml to force the python fallback. 2) if pad token contains unicode glue, map it to '<pad>' in tokenizer.json to avoid mismatch with padding codepaths. 3) OOM on 48GB with micro_batch_size 8 is plausible at seq2048 — try micro_batch_size 4 and bump max_batch_tokens to 4096 for steady latency.

samir: I'm going to run perf sweep across bs=1/4/8/16 and seq=512/1024/2048 on a 48GB node. I'll also test fp16 vs q4_0. Running the bench harness:
```bash
./bench/run_perf.sh --model lumen-13b --weights s3://redwood-models/lumen-13b/v1/weights.pt --tokenizer s3://redwood-models/lumen-13b/v1/tokenizer.json --seq 1024 --batch 8 --iters 200
```
Will post a condensed summary when done.

bench-bot: perf run queued on runner-a100-48 (job id 8421) — estimated 12m. Logs: https://ci/internal/8421

samir: quick observation after first pass (bs1/seq512/fp16): p50=34ms p95=98ms, throughput ~280 tokens/s per GPU, RSS ~24GB.

samir: bs8/seq1024/fp16 (same node): p50=110ms p95=420ms, throughput ~1100 tokens/s aggregated, but observed tail latency spikes correlated with cache prefill. RSS ~38GB (close to limit). queueing happens when many small requests try to share the batch — head-of-line blocking visible in traces.

samir: q4_0 baseline (bs8/seq1024): throughput +8% but p95 worsened by ~15ms, and we saw a few tokenization failures when fast tokenizer was used (non-ascii pad token).

li: notes/suggestions: - set tokenizers.fast=false to avoid the empty-token bug. - in router config use max_batch_tokens=4096 + micro_batch_size=4 to reduce per-GPU memory pressure while keeping batching efficiency. - enable async prefix caching only for long-lived sessions; prefix caching caused uneven mem spikes when many short requests hit cached prefixes.

maya: thanks, will change model.yaml before PR: set micro_batch_size=4, max_batch_tokens=4096, tokenizers.fast=false, and add a tokenizer normalization step to replace unicode pad token. Any objections to adding a small smoke test in CI to token-check newline cases?

samir: +1 to smoke test. Add a quick unit that tokenizes ["Hello\nWorld", "\n", " "] and asserts non-empty outputs and no zero-length tokens. Keeps us honest.

li: I'll draft the PR change and bump the catalog entry metadata with the perf numbers and recommended serving config. Also will add a note: Q4_0 supported but mark as "experimental" due to slight p95 regressions.

maya: awesome — thanks all. tagging @samir for final perf numbers and @li for the PR. I'll wait for bench logs and then open the catalog PR. :thumbsup:
